utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. Please be seated. Good morning, ladies and gentlemen; good morning to the technical booth and the interpreters; good morning to the Prosecution and the Defence counsels. We're going to resume our work where we left off, and I think we have Mr. Fila. Mr. Fila, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, according to our agenda, we were to have the psychiatrist first, I believe, who said he would be coming at 9.00 this morning. But as he doesn't seem to be here, with the Court's indulgence, I should like to begin with the next witness. And the pseudonym for this witness is DC7, and that is the last witness that we will have before this Tribunal with a pseudonym. So may we have Witness DC7 escorted into the courtroom, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness DC7. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am talking to you. I am here in front of you. You will now be reading the solemn declaration handed to you by the usher, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may be seated. Thank you very much for having come, DC7. You will now be answering questions put to you by Mr. Fila, who is the gentleman standing up on your left. Before we commence, please take a look at this piece of paper and tell us whether your name is on the paper. Give us a yes or no answer, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. Very well. Mr. Fila, your witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, may we move into private session for a few moments to hear this witness's particulars.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, let us move into private session, please. You can go ahead now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're in open session now. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Before the war, while you lived and worked in Ljubija, did you happen to meet somebody called Mladjo Radic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: I met Mladjo Radic before the war. He was a policeman. And whenever I needed some law and order put into my premises, I would call Mladjo Radic and the other policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: What was the national composition of Ljubija?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: The national composition of Ljubija is -- there are three nationalities: the Serbs, Croats, and Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: In the conduct of Mladjo Radic, did you notice -- what was Mladjo Radic's conduct towards the members of these three nations? Was there any difference in his behaviour towards them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: He had a good relationship with everybody. He treated everybody the same; all the ethnic groups he treated the same. His behaviour was always proper and he was nice to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I should now like to focus on the time of your arrest.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: I was at home. I was in my house. And one morning - it was on the 14th of July, in the morning, at around 7.00 -- the police came and surrounded my house, and they arrested me and took me off to the police station, myself and another group of people, of Muslims and Croats together. And we were there for interrogation. We stayed there perhaps an hour to an hour and a half, and immediately after that, they sent us to the Keraterm camp. In the Keraterm camp, we stayed for a couple of hours, perhaps until the afternoon, and in the afternoon we were transferred to Omarska. When we arrived in Omarska, we got out, they searched us, frisked us, and then took us to the "white house." In the "white house" there was a room where we waited to be interrogated. When we were waiting around there during the afternoon, a guard came to fetch me and one of my colleagues, and he took us off to the offices on the upper storey for questioning. I stayed there for one or two hours while they questioned me, and after this questioning, they took us back, the two of us. We were in two rooms. They took me out and returned me to the "white house." I was slightly unconscious there, and he threw me into the room and that's where I stayed. That night I spent in that room, and in the morning at about 6.00 a.m., a soldier came and called out my name. I waited for a little while. I didn't respond straight away, but he started shouting, "What are you waiting for?" and took me off and said that I should go and report down there. I came up to him. He turned me round and led me off some 200 metres, down a path. I was unconscious at the time as well. Mladjo met me there and the soldier left. Mladjo took me off a couple of metres. My son was there; he was on a pista. There were more of us there. Those of us who were detained, we were all there, and my son was there too. He told me that I should go off to the young one there, that I would have a better time there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Just for clarification, the witness said twice he was unconscious. Was it because he was sick or was he badly treated? Just to continue understanding.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: I was not ill. I was a healthy man. But because I had been to the interrogation session, I was mistreated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Do you know how Mladjo Radic came to learn that you were located in the "white house"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: I know because my son, a month earlier, had been sent to the camp as well. He was sent to Keraterm and transferred to Omarska. He was there one month before me. So when I arrived, my son saw me on that evening, that afternoon. When they brought me, he saw me in the group of people that were brought there in the evening. And then he must have seen Mladjo who must have been passing there, and he told Mladjo that his father had been brought there to the camp. He said, "See what you can do, please. See if you can get him out of the 'white house' and have him transferred to my group." Mladjo did do that, and he told me that I could go and join my son, that nothing would happen to me, that it would be better for me to be there. That is how I joined my son and was with my son together, right up until we left for Manjaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Let me ask you something else now, Witness. When your son asked Mladjo Radic to help you, what did Mladjo Radic tell him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: When my son asked Mladjo Radic to help me and to get me out of the "white house," Mladic said the following: "I'll do whatever I can, but I can't do anything alone. I must contact my superiors first."

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: When you say "Mladic," who are you thinking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: Well, Krkan.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: In your opinion, what was the importance of the fact that you were transferred from the "white house" to the pista? What Mladjo did for you, how do you assess that? Was that important?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: Could you explain that question to me? I don't quite follow you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: What is the importance? Where was the improvement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: Well, the improvement was because the "white house" was renowned that anybody who found himself in the "white house," it was a very difficult -- the prospects for staying alive were very slight, and they could only stay alive if somebody saved them, like they saved me. I'm walking around today - I'm alive - because I was transferred to my son's group. Mladjo Radic transferred me there. And I have come here to say how it all happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Was your son protected by Mladjo Radic in some way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: Yes, he was, together with me because we were there together. And afterwards, nobody came to abuse us or to call us out as they did others. Other people were called out in that group, but not us. They were called out, taken off, and some of them didn't return. But we were always there in the same place and nobody ever called us out or abused us in any way. So we were safe there. Our security was better there.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Did you talk to the other people from Ljubija about their impressions in connection with Mladjo Radic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: I can say only one thing: While we were there together, our people from Ljubija were there too and the others were in other rooms as well. We couldn't all fit into that same room because there were several hundred of us there. We had to lie down -- we could just lie down. We couldn't move around anywhere or look anywhere. The other people -- Mladjo, whenever he found people from Ljubija -- because he spent some 20 years with us in Ljubija, he knew all the Ljubija inhabitants very well, so whenever he found people from Ljubija, he would take them away from the other rooms and bring them to our room because our room was somehow safer. And I heard from these other people, neighbours of mine, and I asked them, "How come you came here?" And they would all say, "Mladjo transferred me to this room and told me to be there."

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: How many people were there from Ljubija roundabout?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: In my opinion, about 100 people from Ljubija and the surrounding villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: When you talked to the people from Ljubija, did they say that he had helped them as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: Well, yes. We would be lying down and talking to each other. He helped not only one person but many people. Perhaps 20, 30 people.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: How would you assess the conduct of Mladjo Radic as a guard in the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: My opinion is that Mladjo was a good person and he tried to help anybody he could, to try and make the situation better for them. The other people said that he did help. I think that Mladjo was good for others too. For example, he helped me, but he also helped others and saved others, and that is how I am able to say that he was good. I don't think there was any disturbance around him while he was there, while I was in the camp. I wasn't in the camp for a long time, just one month, and then was transferred to Manjaca. But I never heard from anybody that Mladjo was bad towards anybody, nor did I see Mladjo in the compound, that he came like other policemen and soldiers and called people out and sent them off -- and then they were sent off by bus. I never saw Mladjo doing that. I went to the kitchen and I wasn't able to see him there either.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: When you finally went home to Ljubija after Manjaca, did Mladjo Radic come to Ljubija to visit you or others?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: When I was in Omarska, after Omarska I was transferred to Manjaca. There were 17 buses. We were all transferred and we were taken over by the Red Cross there. We had a good time there. Nobody came; no soldiers, no military people came to us after that. A commission turned up one day, the Red Cross Commission. It took down all our names, registered us, particularly us elderly people - (redacted) - they took down our names and the minors as well. There were children underage, below the age of 18. And some 15 days later, we were transferred to Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: But I'm interested about when you got home to Ljubija.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: When I got home to Ljubija, I was at home for five months, and Mladjo came at least 15 times, perhaps more, to the house, but he came at night. He wasn't able to enter my house because there were my Orthodox neighbours there. He didn't dare come into contact with me in my house, but I would go outside. And he would ask me, "Are you all right? Is anybody bothering you?" and I would say, "No." I would say that I was secure and safe. Nobody had taken me off anywhere. And I spent five months at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: In talking to the other people from Ljubija who were not Serbs, that is to say, the Croats and Muslims, did you ever hear that anybody said anything bad about Mladjo Radic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: For all the time I spent at home, nobody told me anything bad about Mladjo Radic. They only told me good things about him.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have completed my questioning of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Fila. Are there any other Defence counsel who wish to question this witness? No? Very well. Mr. Waidyaratne, please. Witness, you are now going to answer questions put to you by the Prosecutor. Mr. Waidyaratne, your witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Witness, I will refer to you as DC7. Please bear with me as you have been given some protective measures. Do you hear me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Were you arrested on the 14th of July, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Who are the people who arrested you? Was it the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: It was the police from Ljubija, our police.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: When you were arrested, did they tell you as to why you were being arrested?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: They arrested me and took me to the police station and I was interrogated there for about an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: They didn't tell you as to why you were arrested; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: They said -- they told me that they were arresting me and that I would be taken to the Omarska camp - because allegedly my son had given some assistance to a Muslim organisation - that they would question me and bring me back home. However, I stayed in Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Were you aware whether your son has given assistance to a Muslim organisation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: I didn't know that. My son is of age.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did he tell you at any time, even in the camp, whether he assisted any Muslim organisation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: He did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Who are the people -- did you recognise any of the policemen who arrested you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: Yes, I did recognise those policemen, because they would come to my cafe, as Mladjo would, at times.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: What are the names, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: Yes. I knew Savo and Zekan.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, Witness, when you were taken to the Omarska camp, there were many others who were taken with you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Were you searched when you arrived in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: Yes, we were. When I set off from Omarska, I asked a policeman in Ljubija to give me half a kilo of bread to put in my pocket, to save it for the camp. Because actually, when we reached Keraterm, where we spent a couple of hours, we were searched immediately, and they didn't leave even that half a kilo of bread on me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Who are the people who searched you at Omarska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: When we arrived at Omarska, there may have been ten or so of us in a vehicle. We got off, and on the spot, before we went to the "white house," we were searched by them as well and then taken to the "white house." I do not know the people who searched us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Were they guards at the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: I think they were guards. They were armed. They searched us and then they took us to this building.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: During the time that you were searched, did they beat you or harass you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Witness, you said that you were taken to the "white house." Who ordered you to go to the "white house"? Who ordered you to go to the "white house"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: When we were questioned, I wasn't conscious, and the same guard who had brought me for interrogation took me to the "white house."

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Please bear with me. I think you didn't understand my question. After your arrival, you said that you were taken to the "white house." Who ordered you to go to the "white house"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: When I arrived, the people who searched us ordered us to go to the "white house." And so they took us there, and after that, we went in for questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: When you were in the "white house," before you were taken for interrogation, you would have seen the people who were in the "white house," the detainees. Did you recognise any of them? Can you name some? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: No, I didn't, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: How did they look? What was the condition of those prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: They were in a bad state, because they went for interrogation and came back to the "white house," and then occasionally they would be taken back there again, back and forth. So they were in a poor condition, as was I, for that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: What you meant by "bad condition" and "poor condition," is that that they were physically not in a good condition, physically they were beaten? Did you see bruises, injuries?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: That's what I had in mind when I say that they were in a bad condition, because that was the condition I was in as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, at the interrogation, when you were taken for interrogation, you said a guard took you, is that correct, for interrogation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: At the interrogation you said -- did they beat you when they questioned you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: At the interrogation, when I arrived, they did hit me. They questioned me and hit me occasionally. And when they finished with the interrogation -- there were two of them. One was a policeman and one from the crime department, and when they had interrogated me, they took me out. And there were three guards out there. They told me to go out. And then they ordered them to take me away and to beat me, and they took me to a room where they beat me quite a bit, and after that, they took me back to the "white house."

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you say "they" beat you. Was it the interrogator or the policeman who beat you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: A policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: And that was in front of the interrogator that they beat you -- that he beat you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, you said that you were taken to the "white house" after the interrogation and you fainted. Was it due to the beating that you fainted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: It was because of the beating. I still have some consequences in my left ear. I have an injury.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Were there visible injuries on you after this beating?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: Not straight away, but later on, when I left home -- I went to Vienna. From Vienna I went to America. When I arrived in America, I had consequences. So that --

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Witness, please bear with me.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: -- my left ear was in poor condition.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Please try to understand the question that I pose to you and answer without giving any details. Witness, then you said after you were -- there was a soldier who came to the "white house" and called your name. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Was it a soldier or a guard who came into the "white house" at that time to call your name? How was he dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: It was a guard, in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: He called your name and took you outside to the pista; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Do you know the person who -- the name of the guard who called you out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Then he took you to the pista and Mr. Radic was there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: And where did Mr. Radic take you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: When I reached Radic I wasn't fully conscious, and I didn't even recognise him until I got quite close up to him. And then the guard left. Probably Radic told him to go to his position. And he escorted me for about 20 metres. We were all there. My son was there too. My son got up. The other detainees were lying down. And my son got up and saw Mladic with me, and Mladic said that I should join my son, which I did. And after that, I didn't see Radic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Witness, Radic took you to a place in the pista; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: Radic took me and told me to go to the pista to join my son and that nobody would hurt me and that I would be safer there than in the "white house." And that is what happened. I joined my son and stayed with him until we went to Manjaca. And I was okay. Nobody hurt me or mistreated me or did anything wrong to me or my son.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, Witness, when you went to the pista and met Radic and he took you to your son, were there any other guards present at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: No, there were no other guards there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: You said today in your evidence that it was in the night that you were called out. Was it in the night or the next day morning that you were called out by the guard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: In the morning. In the morning, about 6.00, between 6.00 and 7.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: So when you were called out, there were guards in the pista during that time; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: No. The guard came to the "white house" to fetch me. He called me out. He took me out of the "white house." I came across Mladic and then he took me to my son, and he told me to join him and stay there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, in the pista, did you see any other guards --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness has answered the same question twice already, Your Honour, or maybe three times, so I wonder how many more times Mr. Waidyaratne intends to ask the same question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: I will move on, Your Honour, but I asked that question again because the witness changed his position that it was in the night and subsequently that it was in the morning. That's why I asked those questions. I will move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Witness, until you left to Manjaca, were you in the pista or did you go to any other room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: During the day, we would be at the pista, and at night we went inside, in the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Who took you to the hangar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: The guards ordered us to go to the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: And in the hangar did you see Mr. Radic? Did he come to see you or any of the prisoners from Ljubija?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: I did not see Radic any other time except when he took me from the "white house" up to my son. After that, I never saw him again, at guard posts or anywhere else. And we couldn't see anyway because we were either in the hangar or at the pista. We had to lie on our stomachs, so we couldn't see people passing by, and I never heard anything about Radic. I knew he had a good reputation. He lived for 20 years amongst us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Please, Witness, answer my question. You don't need to go into details, unnecessary details. Now, Witness, when you left Manjaca, you were taken to Trnopolje; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: And from Manjaca, you returned to Ljubija again; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: You said that Radic came and visited you at least 15 times; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: But that he did it in the night and he didn't want any others --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: Yes, at night.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: -- any others to see you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you ask him as to why he risked his position to come and see you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: I did ask Mladic, "How did you have the courage to come and visit me?" He said, "I came to check that nobody had abused you or mistreated you since you returned home from the camp." He came to check on me several times to make sure I was all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Do you know any others who were detainees that Mr. Radic subsequently, after they were released from the camp, whom Mr. Radic visited?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: I know who were in the camp, but I don't know whether he visited others. He probably visited others too, but I didn't hear about it. You see, I went home. I was released as an elderly man. Others stayed on in the camp; others went abroad and were transferred to Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Please bear with me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Witness, you gave the names of the policemen who arrested you, Savo and Zekan. Do you know their full names, the policemen from Ljubija?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: All I can say is this: Savo and Zekan did not arrest me. Other policemen arrested me who were in Ljubija. Savo and Zekan interrogated me at the police station in Ljubija.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: That concludes my cross-examination. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Waidyaratne. Mr. Fila, any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Witness DC7, just one question for you: During the time you spent in Omarska, some 30 days or so, and when Krkan took you to your son, did you have the impression that he did this overtly or secretly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: When I was in Omarska and when Krkan took me to my son, he couldn't do it in public altogether because his people were watching. He had to sort of conceal it a little bit so that people would not see what he was doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: My last question: Do you have any impression or opinion as to his position in the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: I am not able to say anything about his position in Omarska, but I viewed him as an ordinary guard. He wore a uniform, and sometimes he was a guard providing security of the camp itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour. That's all for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Fila. Judge Fouad Riad, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Witness DC7, good morning. Can you hear my voice? Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: Yes, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I gather from what you've said that you were an old friend of Mr. Radic. You have known him for a long time; is this right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: The friendship of Mr. Radic, did it continue with you even after the beginning of the ethnic conflict, or did you stay away from each other?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: Our friendship existed from before this started in our country, because he worked, as far as I know, for 20 years as a policeman in our area and he would always come to establish order in the cafe that I ran. We always were on good terms, even afterwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I mean even after the start of the conflict.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: Yes. When the conflict started too, we were on good terms. We were always on good terms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned that you were mistreated in the interrogation. At that time, was Mr. Radic --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: -- aware of your presence in the camp, or was it before he knew about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: Mr. Radic was not in the camp that day when I arrived. It was only in the evening that he learnt that I had arrived at the camp. He learnt it from my son and the other people from Ljubija who were in the camp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So after he learnt about your presence, there was no mistreatment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: There was none, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You said that your son was on the pista and you went to the "white house." Wasn't it your son who was helping --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: -- or financing some Muslim funds and organisations? What was the main crime for your son?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: The main charges against my son, he went to the camp a month before me, and they were saying that he had assisted this Muslim organisation and things like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And you went to the camp because of your son.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that was what they said, apparently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So the fact that you went to the "white house" and you were not charged with the same accusation, you went -- they put you in the "white house" and your son was in the pista. Was that also due to Mr. Radic's influence? Yes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: He was taken away a month prior to me and he was first in Keraterm, then in Omarska. Then when I arrived, when I was taken to Omarska, he had already been interrogated, all that was behind him, and he was on the pista and in the hangar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: On the pista also thanks to Mr. Radic's intervention?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned that Mr. Radic never called people out, you never saw him on the compound, and you never saw him in the kitchen. Where was he? Don't the guards go around these places?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: We would go to the kitchen once in 24 hours. We would get one meal. I never noticed him there at the time in the kitchen or at the pista. He didn't pass by. Some guards did pass by but he didn't. Where he was, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: The guards who passed by, were they just the simple guards or were they people of certain importance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: Well, you see, there were ordinary guards and there were also some policemen, but I didn't know any of them. I saw them pass by. Because we always had to lie down, we couldn't really look around much. We weren't standing up to be able to see everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Did you have an idea while you were there who was in charge of the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: I could not tell you, nor did I hear who was in charge in the camp because I just didn't know that. I wasn't there for long. After that, we went to Manjaca.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Because Mr. Radic told you that he would have to ask the superior to transfer you. Did he mention to you who was the superior?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Judge Fouad Riad. Madam Judge Wald.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Witness DC7, following up on Judge Riad's question, you said that when Mr. Radic first talked to you, he said he would try to help you get out of the "white house" but he would have to contact his superiors. I think you testified to that. Then later, in answer to a question, you said that when Mr. Radic took you to the pista, to your son, he had to do it not in the open so that people wouldn't see him too much. Did you have the impression or did you know whether or not, when he did take you to your son and get you out of the "white house," he did that by himself or he had gone to his superiors and gotten permission to do that? Mr. Fila is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I wouldn't have any objections, but Judge Riad and now Judge Wald are misinterpreting the witness's statement. Mr. Radic told his son this thing about the command in the camp, not to the witness. Both questions were asked on the basis of something that the witness had not said. Will you please check the transcript? It was his son that Radic told that he had to ask the superiors, not the witness. This is the second time that we are following the wrong path.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Fila, I believe that Judge Wald has the right to ask this question. In the end, you will have the floor and will be able to say whatever you like. Yes, Judge Wald.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I would like to just repeat the basic question at the end. When Mr. Radic took you to your son, along with the guard at the pista, was it your impression - because you said he didn't do it -- the translation was openly - was it your impression that he was doing that on his own or he was doing it with the approval of whoever those in charge of the camp were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: When Radic took me to my son, he was not near us. He was on the road that was there between us. He took me to that road and told me to go to my son. Because I could see my son, he told me to move on to my son and that I would be with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: So you didn't have any impression as to whether or not he was doing that on his own authority or with the approval of whoever ran the camp.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DC7
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not have any questions. Mr. Fila, has the matter been clarified now? Yes, thank you. Very well. Witness, since I do not have any questions for you, we should like to thank you for coming here and we wish you a happy return to where you reside. Will the usher now help you leave the courtroom. Thank you. Just don't move for awhile.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I do not know whether the psychiatrist has arrived. If he has, then we should hear him. If he hasn't, then we have the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We shall see now whether he is here or not.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I have just spoken with Victims and Witness Section and he has not arrived as of yet, so they're bringing up the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Could Radovan Medic please be called.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Somers, do you agree with this sequence or do you have any comments?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Fila was kind enough to tell me this morning about the problem, and we have agreed that whenever -- if ever this individual arrives, we'll proceed. We thank him very much for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Fila, before we begin, is this a protected witness or not? Because if not, then we have to put up the curtains.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Until the end of the week, there will be no other protected witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Then we can pull the screens up. Witness, will you stand up, please. So this is Mr. Radovan Medic [Realtime transcript read in error "Mr. Radic van Medic"]. Good morning. You will now read the solemn declaration which the usher will give you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: There must be some mistake in the name. It says "Mr. Radic Medic."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Medic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: The first --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Radovan Medic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So there is no Radic. All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. There is no problem. I trust this will be corrected. So this is Mr. Radovan Medic. Thank you for coming here. Now you will answer questions that Mr. Fila will be asking of you. Mr. Fila, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Mr. Radovan Medic, where were you born and when?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: I did not hear you. I cannot hear anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: Yes, now I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Mr. Medic, where and when were you born?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: I was born on the 7th of January, 1954, in Bosanski Novi.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: And where do you live now?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: Now I live in Prijedor, Herzegovacka 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: What are you?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: I am a car mechanic, but I work as a driver.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel and witness please pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: And your ethnicity is?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: And you are of Orthodox faith?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Will the counsel and witness please pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Did you work for Autotransport before the war?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did, and I work there to this day. I still work there.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Do you have a family?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: I have a wife and two sons.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Have you ever been convicted?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: While you worked -- during your career at Autotransport Prijedor before the war, did you meet a person called (redacted)

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: (redacted) (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Now we shall move on to 1991. Where were you in September 1991 and what position did you hold?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: In September I was in West Slavonia. The place is called Bijele Stijene, near Lipik, and I was deputy chief responsible for security of the Motorised Brigade, of the 343rd Motorised Brigade, and I was also the chief commander's driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Did you have a rank, and which one?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: When I entered the war, I was a Captain.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: And when you left the war?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: I was a Major.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Will the counsel and witness please pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: And since you were a military policeman, did you have any powers regarding transgressions, incidents, thefts by JNA soldiers?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was my only duty. I was responsible for that form of crime in the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: And who was the head of security, the chief of security?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: The chief of security. The chief of security was Ranko Babic, Captain First Class Ranko Babic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: When in that area around Lipik did you come across (redacted) again, and what was she doing then?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: I did come across her towards the end of November or in early December. I'm not quite sure. (redacted) (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: As a volunteer in the Yugoslav People's Army, was she a combatant? Did the Yugoslav People's Army mobilise women?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: No, the Yugoslav People's Army did not mobilise women. She had applied as a volunteer. There were two or three women in that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Will you now explain to us the incident which happened with regard to some theft.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: As I have already mentioned, in late November or early December, a complaint arrived for four or five inhabitants there of Croat ethnicity. They came to report burglaries and theft of the inventory, that is, of technical goods. And the chief of security ordered me to go to the scene to see what had happened. And as we investigated in a bus, we found a large number of these technical goods there, that is, television, microwave ovens, and so on and so forth. That bus was responsibility [as interpreted] and it was driven by Miodrag Kicanovic. And I tried to find, on the basis of documents, to see who was responsible for what, and then I looked for that Kicanovic. When I found him and asked him, "What's this in the bus?" he said, "Oh, nothing. Give me the keys." And I took him to the bus, but he did not have the keys because (redacted) had the key.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Did (redacted) use that bus for a purpose?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: Miodrag Kicanovic has given the bus to (redacted) to sleep in it, and (redacted) and in another unit there were two more women, so that she wouldn't sleep with the rest. And then we found (redacted), and she said afterwards that those things did not belong to her. But then some people recognised her, and a soldier -- (redacted). I'm not sure. (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Did you make photocopies of all those documents? Did you keep them and then turn them over to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: I turned over all the originals, as I had to, and I copied only the documents which I needed so that I would keep -- I wanted to keep them as my protection in view of the developments.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should like to ask the usher to get three documents: D15/3A and D15/3B, and then D16 and D17.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: What are they about, Witness?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: This is the official record which was drawn up for the military police in the command, that is, the military police in the locality called Bijele Stijene.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: And who signed the document?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: I signed this document on behalf of the chief of security because he was absent and I was authorised by him to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Are there any other signatures here?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: There is also the signature of (redacted) and Miodrag Kicanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Does he -- does she say in this document that she had robbed the objects found in the bus?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: Yes. But then a criminal record -- a criminal report was done. This was only the record, the official record of what had been found at the scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can take those documents back, and bring document D16/3A and D16/3B.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: What are these documents about; will you tell us? Is that the document that you handed over?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: This was the criminal report; that is, Ranko Babic was succeeded by Captain First Class Zvonko --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me. We still do not have the document on the ELMO. Does the Prosecution have the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, we do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I've just checked my records and the document is confidential.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it is not confidential. Could the usher please put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Fila, just a moment. We see that the document is marked as confidential and therefore we have to check that properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I can put it in a very cautious manner. Is that the criminal report filed on the basis of the official record that the witness submitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. Fila, Madam Registrar will see about this document because this document was filed as a confidential document. I do not really know why was it filed as such. But if it is confidential, we cannot show it, unless the decision to have if filed as confidential is changed. Do you know anything about why it was filed as confidential?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe, Mr. President, that this is because it was during the interrogation of an individual, of a protected individual. But I did not ask that it be made confidential.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not really remember, but it is true that it has to be verified. Madam Registrar gave me the document and I saw that it was marked confidential. So perhaps we can examine it in a private session, as a precautionary measure. Can we move into private session now, please, and I will ask the usher to use the ELMO. The witness needs to verify the document on the ELMO, but you will adjust the position of the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do other Defence counsel have any other questions to ask of this witness? Mr. Simic, do you have any questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I see that other counsel do not have other questions. Do you have questions, Judge Wald? Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Saxon, your witness. Please go ahead with the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I just want to mention that in the last document we had on the ELMO, there was a confusion between "she" and "he." Sometimes they would say "he." So I want to make sure that the "he" was a reference to the "she," or it was another person. This is a verification which can be done again. The last document we had on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right, Your Honour, I will try to get to that last document and ask the witness to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Medic, before Mr. Fila began to ask you questions, you took an oath today to tell the whole truth and nothing but the truth. Do you stand by everything that you have told the Trial Chamber this morning?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You mentioned that for a number of years now you've been working as a driver for the Autotransport company. Is that the company that operates buses in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: It is the company that renders services of all kind; the transport of people, goods. It deals in cars, repairs, and everything to do with traffic and vehicles. It encompasses all that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: During May/June of 1992, were you working for the Autotransport company as a driver?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Were you working as a mechanic?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: No. At that time, I was on the battlefield.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You mentioned that when you were serving in Croatia in 1991, that there was an incident that occurred, according to you, at the end of November or early December regarding (redacted). Do you recall describing that incident?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: I remember that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If the usher could place Exhibit D15/3B back on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You have the B/C/S version in front of you; is that correct, Mr. Medic?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: At the top of the page, we see the words "Lieutenant Radovan Medic." That was you, was it not, or is you?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This report or official note is a report of an investigation into the incident that you described that occurred in November/December 1991; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Trial Chamber why this report, this official note, is dated 16 October 1991? How is it that a report regarding an incident that occurred at the end of November or December 1991 was compiled at least a month before the incident happened? Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: You didn't understand me. But please could you repeat your question? It's not quite clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You testified today several times that this alleged incident involving (redacted) occurred in Croatia, in an area known as Lipik, at the end of November or in December of 1991. Defence counsel has asked you to comment upon an official note which you allegedly compiled regarding that alleged incident. This official note is dated 16 October 1991, what's in front of you right now. I'm asking you, how was it that you were able to work on an investigation of an incident that allegedly occurred in October 1991, compile a report, if the incident did not occur until late November or early December 1991? Can you explain that, please?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: The incident occurred on the date when this official note was written, in Donji Caglic. I could not remember whether it was the end of October, the beginning of November, or whatever, because it was a long time ago. But the document is dated the 16th of October, when it was compiled. And then the proceedings ensued and she was investigated, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I just want to understand you. You come into this courtroom today in public and you make allegations about a person in public and you talk about the date when this alleged incident happened in public, and now you tell us, well, you can't really remember the date when the incident occurred. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: The incident occurred at the end of September -- at the end of October or mid-October. That was when it happened. I can't remember. It's 10 or 11 years ago and it's difficult to remember the dates, when what happened. It was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Saxon, there seems to be some confusion. I have ordered that the transcript be redacted, because the document that was placed on the ELMO was confidential; it is a confidential document. So I have issued orders that the transcript be redacted and it be deleted from the LiveNote. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, and I apologise for any inconvenience that I have caused. While we're on the subject of this confidential document, if I could ask -- I'm going to move backward. The witness was beginning to answer a question, but I don't think he had the time to finish his question [sic].

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Medic, you began to say, "At that time during the combat, my sons were minors," and then we had to take a short pause. Is there anything more you want to say in answer to your question?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: I was only afraid because my sons were minors, they were underage, and I was told, "Watch out what you're doing, because somebody could take your child."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Is it your testimony today that the production of an alleged criminal report about theft of some, as you put it, technical items, was going to place your sons at risk and that's why you needed to keep copies of these reports?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: It wasn't the theft that was a danger, but those people who had perpetrated this, who took part in those things.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So how could keeping photocopies of reports that you wrote about such a theft provide you with protection or provide your sons with protection?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: The original documents were handed over in regular fashion. If I told the perpetrators that I had the document and that I hadn't handed it in and shown them the photocopy, then they thought that I was their man and that I would protect them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I will move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we place document D16/3B again on the ELMO, and I understand it is a confidential document. I would retract that. If the B/C/S version of this document can simply be shown to the witness one more time so that we don't have further problems with confidentiality. I have a language question to ask the witness that I hope will also clear up the question that Judge Riad asked at the beginning. Or we could go into private session for one moment, Your Honour. It is up to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Saxon, how much time do you need to complete your cross-examination, roughly? Because I'm looking at the clock and see that it's 11.00, so we should take a break round about now. We have been working for some time. How much more do you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I believe I could do it in about two minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean the whole of your cross-examination, to complete it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. Very well. Let us have -- give the document to the witness without placing it on the ELMO. Hand him the document in B/C/S. Is that what you wish, Mr. Saxon?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: May we please go into private session, Your Honour. I've been informed that I need to have this document on the ELMO so that the interpreters can see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Let us move into private session for a few moments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in open session. Please proceed, Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Medic, ten years have gone by since that particular event. Was your memory better today and what you said today, or what was written there in --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: What was written there is better. Ten years later I am not able to remember all the details, because I had very many similar cases, cases of that kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You gave a statement to Zoran Jovanovic?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then you said that it was in mid-October. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And my last question: What you read out, the document in closed session, you said that it was a form, a standard form. What do we mean by "standard form"?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: It means a form, a document which the information service can give to the Security Service, and the document is printed both for male and female, because we had women in the army as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The document says "military conscript."

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: Yes, she is a military conscript, but she was a volunteer. She joined the Yugoslav People's Army on a voluntary basis and expressly asked to be sent to the battleground.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And my last question: Did you compile that form or was the form compiled by someone else?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: I signed the form, but usually you dictate it to a typist or somebody like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But you received this standard form?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: Yes. The form is a standard form, typewritten, and you just cross out or leave in whether it is he or she, depending on the criminal report being made.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Fila. Madam Judge Wald has the floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I have two questions. For the second one, I think maybe to avoid confusion, it's better to go into private session. The first one is simply this: Were you actually in the presence (redacted)? I mean, were you there? Did you hear her? You actually heard her confess?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN MEDIC
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. I just wanted to clarify that. Could we go into private session for just one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Radovan Medic, we have no further questions for you. We thank you for coming to the Tribunal and wish you a safe return back to your place of residence. I am now going to ask the usher to accompany you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should like to thank you too. I did not answer the question put to me by the gentleman here that I am accusing somebody. I am just presenting the facts, the facts that I witnessed. I am not accusing anybody, nor am I authorised to accuse anybody.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us now take a half-hour break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated. Mr. Fila, I think the next witness is Miodrag Kicanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, unless the psychiatrist has arrived in the meantime. In that case, yes, Miodrag.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Kicanovic. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I hear you extremely well. Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You are now going to read the solemn declaration that the usher is going to give you, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Approach the microphones, please, a little. That's fine now. First you will be answering questions put to you by Mr. Fila. Mr. Fila, your witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. You are Miodrag Kicanovic, are you not?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: When and where were you born?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: In 1941, in Raca, near Bijeljina, on the 9th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: By ethnicity, you are?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: A Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Of Orthodox faith?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: What are you by trade?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: I am a professional driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Do you have a family?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: I am married and have two children.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Before the beginning of the war, you were living in Prijedor, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Where were you working at the time?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: In Autotransport Prijedor, as a bus driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: From when until when?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: From 1971 until 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: And then you moved to where?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: In 1993, I moved to Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: While you were working in Autotransport in Prijedor as a bus driver, did you meet a person called (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: (redacted) (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Did you visit each other? Were you friends?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we were very close. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: (redacted) (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: (redacted) (redacted).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Waidyaratne.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: I object to this question, Your Honour. Mr. Fila is asking for a general opinion of this witness; not even the opinion of this witness but a general opinion. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't want to keep you. I wanted to save some time so let me rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Do you know whether any proceedings were conducted against her during her employment?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were criminal proceedings because she was taking money from passengers without giving them tickets for it in return.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Were any disciplinary proceedings conducted against her?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the company.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Were you aware of that at the time?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: I learnt afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Did you take care that it should not happen?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. When she worked with me, it never happened. But when she worked with other colleagues, it did happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Let us now focus on 1991. Can you tell us whether you were in Lipik, and why?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: I was because I was in the JNA as a bus driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Did you meet that person there again, (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: What was she doing there?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Was she a member of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, she was. (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Would she sometimes use your bus?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, because my superior said I had to give her the key. All of us who were in the reserve at the time, in the unit, we could use this bus for personal needs, for sleeping in it. I slept there sometimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Can you tell us about an incident linked to Radovan Medic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I don't want to lead you. Just tell us in your own words what happened.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: It was either in October or November. I can't remember exactly. I know it was in autumn. Radovan Medic came and called me and several other policemen - I can't remember how many - asking me what I had in the bus. I said I had no idea. Then he said, "Where is your key?" and I said, "I gave the key to (redacted). Somebody went to find her. She opened the bus, and in the bus we were astonished. There were TV sets and various other appliances. I don't know how many of them, there were so many.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Did Radovan Medic tell you what he had done about it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't hear half of your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Was is it established who had put these goods in the bus, these TV sets, recorders, and so on?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: (redacted) (redacted), so that he didn't bother me any more, nor did he press any charges against me, because people had told him I had nothing to do with those goods. I had just given her the key. (redacted), what she put in the bus. I had no idea. And only when we unlocked it did we realise and see what was inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Was it established who had put the stuff in the bus?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was established that it was (redacted), with some other people. I don't know who they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: And where did those goods come from?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: They came from abandoned houses in Croatia, from Lipik and the surroundings.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that they had been stolen?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I would, of course. What else? Because if there's no one in the house and you collect the stuff from inside, what else can it be called but theft?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a bit leading. Please rephrase the question, Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Do you know the origin of those goods? Can you tell us where those goods came from?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: You don't mean the trademarks, do you? They were TV sets, video recorders, and other appliances from abandoned houses in Croatia, Croatian houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: How did they find their way to the bus?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: Because she went with some other men; I don't know who. They collected the stuff, brought it there, and put it in the bus. They used the truck that she drove during the night. They were not in the compound at all, and it was not my job to check where people were going. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: This was towards the end of 1991, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, in 1991, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Do you know roughly what month it was?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: October or November, something like that. I can't recollect exactly, but I know it was in the autumn.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: After that, did you see or hear anything about (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: No. From that day on, the day the incident occurred, I never saw or heard about her again, to this day.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Do you perhaps know whether she told any stories in Prijedor about what had happened?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: On one occasion I was away on business. I came back and some friends told me that she had said certain things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Waidyaratne.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: This is also speculation, Your Honour. Mr. Fila is getting this witness to speculate and speak about hearsay, and there is no basis for this answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, you allowed Mr. Saxon to ask about something that an investigator heard from another witness, one of his investigators; not from another witness, but from an investigator who spoke to a witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So please continue. Ask the witness whether he heard anything so it's not speculation. To hear is not speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Did you hear that (redacted) had told some stories about you and about this incident?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: I heard it from others, but I specifically did not see anything, but I heard from friends that she had told some stories. But I don't know the exact contents. No one can tell me the exact substance of what she said.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Did she say anything about your role in that event?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. It wasn't I myself that heard her say things. Some people said one story, others another story, so I never managed to get to the bottom of it, what was the truth of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: But did she say that you had reported her or something to that effect?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: She may have. I don't know. Perhaps because I would not accept any guilt for assuming upon myself any part of the blame for something I hadn't done.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Did you hear that she was angry at you because of this?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: She probably was angry, because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: The witness clearly said, "She may have. I don't know," and Mr. Fila is putting the same question again to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This time Mr. Waidyaratne is right, and I withdraw the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Rephrase it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: In the course of 1992, did you ever see (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: What would be your comment if somebody were to establish that you had raped her in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG KICANOVIC
utterances.text: I spent very little time in Prijedor, because I was a driver and I was driving around a lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no further questions.
